rationale:
Second batch of handler-side commit_sha standardisation for bugs_open/334 (RFC_029 step 5's real gate), following migration 519 (page-rerender, submitted, awaiting verdict). Same mechanism, same council-approved shape: section-editor is a real, live bdl handler (confirmed against site_work_items.handler_agent, the top-level dispatch column, not a static list) with its own direct git_commit step. GENUINE JUDGEMENT CALL, stated explicitly in the file: section-editor has TWO git-touching events per run — its own direct commit (deploy_page, output_field git_result, the section edit itself) and a LATER call to deployer-agent (trigger_deploy, output_field deploy_result, described in the live config as "Trigger Cloudflare deployment" — a fleet-wide deployment ping, not this item's own edit). This migration maps commit_sha to git_result (the edit's own commit), not the later trigger's result, on the principle: map to the handler's OWN direct commit, never a nested/downstream call's. deploy_result is left as a plain identity mapping, unchanged.

Same conversion as 519 and the same reason it is required, not merely convenient: section-editor's `complete` step currently uses `output_fields` (list mode), which uses each entry as both the extraction path and the response key — a dotted path added to the list would produce a response key that is that literal string, invisible to any dot-path reader. `result_mapping` is the only mode that builds an independently-named target<-source map, and it is mutually exclusive with `output_fields`. So this is a controlled conversion: every currently-exposed field re-declared as an identity mapping (byte-identical response for existing readers), plus one new `commit_sha` entry.

plan.risks:
1. Same standing risk as 519: I am asserting no existing reader depends on the output_fields shape specifically rather than just the keys/values it produces. result_mapping reproduces byte-identical output for every identity-mapped field.

2. This is one of ~7 real handlers; the flip itself is not touched by this submission. bdl still resolves commit_sha via the search until every handler converts and the bugfix_315 lane adds its wire afterward.


3. THE git_result vs deploy_result CHOICE IS A JUDGEMENT CALL, not a mechanical fact like the other four migrations in this batch. If "the commit that satisfied this item" should instead mean the LATER Cloudflare-triggered one, this migration maps the wrong field. I have stated my reasoning (the work item is the section edit; the edit's own commit is what most naturally answers "which commit satisfied this item") but this is the one submission in the batch where a reviewer's disagreement on interpretation, not on mechanism, would be the right reason to REVISE.
